one_liner: FCL hard fork (formerly HPP-FCL) with rewritten and Nesterov/Polyak-accelerated GJK/EPA; narrow-phase convex queries several times faster than FCL, libccd and Bullet.
what_it_does: A C++ collision and distance library for robotics. It handles primitives (box, sphere, capsule, cylinder, cone, ellipsoid, plane, halfspace), convex hulls, BVH meshes, height fields and octrees, with safety margins, contact points and contact patches. The API resembles FCL's (coal::collide / coal::distance with request and result structs, plus a reintroduced FCL 0.7 broad phase) but lives in the coal:: namespace with its own types; an optional HPP-FCL compatibility header layer covers code written against hpp-fcl. Python bindings exist through Boost.Python/eigenpy and, newer, nanobind.
how_it_is_fast: Coal replaces FCL's libccd-based narrow phase with its own GJK (Van den Bergen-style convergence by default, with duality-gap or hybrid criteria available) and EPA. Its GJK++ work (IEEE T-RO 2024) treats GJK as a Frank-Wolfe method and adds Polyak and Nesterov momentum (GJKVariant::PolyakAcceleration / NesterovAcceleration), which the README and the paper say gives up to about 2x over vanilla GJK. Support-function hints, cached or AABB-based initial guesses (GJKInitialGuess::CachedGuess / BoundingVolumeGuess) and early stop on a distance threshold cut iterations further when queries repeat, as they do in simulation and planning loops.
when_to_use: Many convex-vs-convex collision or distance queries per step (robot links against convex hulls or primitives) where FCL's or libccd's GJK is the hot spot; the README chart puts Coal's Nesterov GJK at about 1.1 us median against about 9.5 us for FCL and 4.2 us for libccd.
Simulation, MPC or motion-planning loops with temporal coherence, where cached GJK guesses and support hints carry over between consecutive queries.
You need a distance lower bound when there is no collision, safety margins, or contact patches for contact-rich simulation; FCL does not provide these.
Stacks already built on Pinocchio, Crocoddyl, HPP or TSID, which depend on Coal and ship it on conda-forge, PyPI and ROS.
when_not_to_use: Broad-phase-heavy scenes of triangle-mesh BVHs: a third-party report (issue #857, GCC 11 -O3, Eigen 3.4) measured Coal 3.0.2's broad phase at 1.71-1.87x slower than FCL 0.6.1 and pairwise distance at 1.08-1.13x slower, with single-pair narrow phase about equal.

Large non-convex mesh-vs-mesh overlap: issue #649 profiles EPA::reset allocations at 1.3 s of a 2.4 s coal::overlap between 5,000- and 4,200-vertex meshes, and the reporter found FCL 0.7 faster there. The issue is still open.
Lightweight or embedded builds: it needs Eigen, Boost (serialization, filesystem) and assimp, with octomap and qhull optional, and builds as a shared library.
When you need audited benchmark numbers: the 5-15x chart states no hardware, compiler or shape set, and against libccd the median gap is about 3.8x, not 5x.
General computational geometry (polygon booleans, triangulation, spatial indexing): Coal is a narrow-phase collision library, not a CGAL, Boost.Geometry or GEOS replacement.

integration.form: shared lib (CMake via jrl-cmakemodules; conda-forge, PyPI 'coal', ROS package, Docker image)
integration.dependencies: Eigen3, Boost (serialization, filesystem; Boost.Log only with COAL_ENABLE_LOGGING), assimp; optional octomap >= 1.8, qhull, Tracy; Python bindings need eigenpy/Boost.Python or nanobind
integration.platforms: Linux, macOS and Windows per CI and packaging (Windows support credited in the README); no ISA-specific requirement documented
integration.thread_safety: Not documented. Free coal::collide/distance calls take caller-owned request and result objects. A ComputeCollision functor holds a mutable GJKSolver, so give each thread its own functor.
integration.drop_in_for_baseline: partial: FCL-like request/result API and the broad phase is FCL 0.7's, but it uses the coal:: namespace, Eigen-based types (Vec3s, Transform3s) and different shape classes, so FCL code must be ported

gotchas: The accelerated GJK is opt-in: CollisionRequest defaults to gjk_variant = DefaultGJK and gjk_initial_guess = DefaultGuess, so you must set NesterovAcceleration (and ideally CachedGuess) to get the headline numbers.
BoundingVolumeGuess silently needs computeLocalAABB() to have been called on both shapes (header warning).

The Box support function used a function-local static inflation factor, so box query results depended on which query ran first in the process (issue #894, fixed by #895 in Sept 2026, listed as unreleased after 3.0.4). The effect is a relative 1e-10 inflation, but results were order-dependent.
Reuse CollisionResult only after calling clear(), and note that penetration_depth excludes the security margin (README example).
pick_this_over_siblings_when: None of the catalogued geometry siblings does rigid-body collision. Of the ones that come close, trueform and Manifold do mesh booleans and queries, and TinyBVH and madmann91/bvh do ray-tracing BVHs. Pick Coal when the workload is GJK/EPA distance and contact between convex robot geometry.
verified_claims_summary: A README box plot (log scale; hardware, compiler and shape set not stated) gives per-query GJK median times of about 1.1 us (Nesterov), 1.2 us (Polyak) and 1.6 us (vanilla Coal), against about 4.2 us for libccd, 9.5 us for FCL and 17 us for Bullet. That is roughly 8.6x over FCL and 3.8x over libccd for the accelerated variant (derived from page data). The underlying GJK++ T-RO 2024 paper claims only up to 2x over the prior state of the art, since that comparison is against vanilla GJK.
status_note: Actively developed by Inria and LAAS-CNRS (3,877 commits, last commit 2026-09-30, release 3.0.4 in June 2026) and BSD-3-Clause, but a heavy dependency set means you link it rather than vendor it.
